text: An LLM call isn't deterministic — the same prompt can return a different answer every time. The only way to debug a bad response after the fact is to see exactly what was sent and exactly what came back.
A useful log entry is more than prompt-in, text-out: request ID and timestamp, model and version, the actual input and output, tokens, latency, cost, status, and a user or session ID.

Here's what that looks like captured in full — the complete chat body, model, token count, latency, and status for one real logged call. Your log store can quietly become the most sensitive database in your stack.
At production volume — millions of calls a month — a log you can't filter is close to useless. Filtering by status, user, or model turns a flood of logged calls into the one that actually matters.

The fix isn't to stop logging — it's choosing, deliberately, what gets captured. Normal, Omit Request, Omit Response, or Omit Both, set per endpoint, so a team keeps detail where it's safe and strips it where it isn't.
Omitting the body doesn't mean flying blind. Status, model, latency, and cost keep flowing even when the prompt and response text themselves are dropped.
Capture enough to debug, strip what you don't need to keep. Next up: turning that same logged metadata into cost and latency tracking you can actually watch.
